title: Industrial Safety
description: Industrial hazards and the organisation of safe work. Lifting equipment, pressure equipment and electrical installations. Accident prevention, worker actions and production control.

sources.file: Презентация вебинара Электробезопасность - Ким - ноябрь 2025 года.pptx

sources.title: Правила эксплуатации оборудования под давлением, приказ № 358
Правила техники безопасности при эксплуатации электроустановок потребителей, приказ № 222

slides.title: Industrial Safety
body: Industrial hazards and the organisation of safe work.
Lifting equipment, pressure equipment and electrical installations.
Accident prevention, worker actions and production control.
slides.callout: A training course for work in the Republic of Kazakhstan.

slides.title: What the course covers
body: General requirements apply across production operations.
Each equipment section covers documentation, authorisation and protective measures.
Practical scenarios help identify conditions that require work to stop.
slides.callout: Equipment-specific authorisation is arranged separately.

slides.title: Purpose of industrial safety
body: Industrial safety protects people, property and the environment from hazardous production factors.
Accident prevention begins before equipment starts.
Emergency preparedness includes communication, evacuation and rehearsed personnel actions.
slides.callout: Safety must be maintained throughout the equipment life cycle.

slides.title: Regulatory framework
body: The Kazakhstan Law on Civil Protection establishes general requirements.
Order No. 359 covers lifting equipment; Order No. 358 covers pressure equipment.
Electrical safety and hot work are governed by their specific rules.
Work instructions account for the equipment and site conditions.
slides.callout: A sample instruction cannot replace requirements for the actual task.

slides.title: Hazardous production facilities
body: Hazardous substances and processes require checking the criteria for a hazardous facility.
Identification follows legislation rather than the everyday name of a business.
Hazardous technical devices are assessed according to their type and parameters.
Workers must know their area's hazards and the limits of their authorisation.
slides.callout: A facility name without the word hazardous does not remove the risk.

slides.title: Hazardous substances and processes
body: Combustible substances can ignite; oxidisers intensify combustion.
Toxic substances are hazardous through inhalation and contact.
Pressure, temperature and mechanical energy can cause severe injury.
Work requires information about the substance, process and protective measures.
slides.callout: Hazards depend on properties and handling conditions.

slides.title: Accidents and incidents
body: Destruction, an uncontrolled explosion or a hazardous release can indicate an accident.
Equipment failure or a process deviation can constitute an incident.
An event must be reported and examined even if nobody is injured.
Concealing a deviation prevents the organisation from averting a later accident.
slides.callout: Record deviations before they recur.

slides.title: Duties of the organisation
body: The organisation maintains equipment and meets mandatory requirements.
It appoints responsible persons and establishes control procedures.
It arranges training, knowledge assessment and personnel authorisation.
It maintains readiness to contain accidents and deal with their consequences.
slides.callout: Appointing a responsible person does not remove the organisation's duties.

slides.title: Worker actions
body: Workers perform assigned tasks within their training and authorisation.
They check the workplace and use the specified protective equipment.
They report defects, deviations and threats to people.
In immediate danger, they stop work and move to safety.
slides.callout: Do not attempt an unauthorised repair of a dangerous fault.

slides.title: Training and authorisation
body: Training explains hazards and safe work methods.
Knowledge assessment verifies understanding of requirements.
A briefing addresses the actual task and workplace.
Practical preparation and authorisation are required where stipulated by the rules and task.
slides.callout: Viewing a presentation does not authorise every operation.

slides.title: Production control
body: Control identifies breaches before an accident occurs.
Checks cover equipment, documentation, personnel and working conditions.
Each finding receives an action, an owner and a deadline.
Closure requires verification that the issue has actually been corrected.
slides.callout: A closed finding needs confirmation on site.

slides.title: Checks before starting work
body: Clarify the task, work-zone boundaries and responsible persons.
Check equipment, protective devices and clear access routes.
Assess neighbouring activities and possible changes in conditions.
Do not begin until unsuitable conditions have been corrected.
slides.callout: Yesterday's good condition does not replace today's check.

slides.title: Workplace risk assessment
body: Identify what could cause harm and who could enter the danger zone.
Prefer hazard elimination and engineering protection.
Organisational measures and PPE provide additional protection.
Repeat the assessment when equipment, tasks or surroundings change.
slides.callout: Changed conditions require a new assessment.

slides.title: Work permits and coordination
body: Use a work permit where required by the rules and established procedures.
Specify the location, task, personnel and protective measures.
Actual workplace conditions must match the conditions of authorisation.
A changed task requires review of the permit conditions, not an informal agreement.
slides.callout: A signature on a permit does not replace completed protective measures.

slides.title: Isolation of energy sources
body: Before maintenance, identify electrical, mechanical and stored energy.
Stop equipment and prevent unintended starting.
Release pressure and secure moving parts under the established procedure.
Authorised personnel verify the absence of hazardous energy.
slides.callout: The Stop button alone does not isolate energy.

slides.title: Hot work
body: Welding, cutting and heating produce sparks and hot surfaces.
Remove combustible materials or protect them using the specified method.
Check adjacent rooms, openings and concealed spaces.
Provide firefighting equipment and post-work monitoring.
slides.callout: Sparks can travel beyond the visible work area.

slides.title: Equipment documentation
body: The equipment passport identifies the device and its permitted parameters.
The manufacturer's manual defines operating and maintenance conditions.
Logs preserve inspection, repair and defect records.
Establish unknown parameters before operating equipment.
slides.callout: A nearby device's parameters cannot replace the equipment passport.

slides.title: Lifting equipment
body: Cranes, hoists and other lifting devices have different applications.
Slings, lifting beams and containers form part of the lifting system.
Equipment selection depends on load mass, the work zone and installation conditions.
Plan the operation using the equipment passport and lifting procedure.
slides.callout: Safe lifting depends on the entire system.

slides.title: Lifting equipment passport and markings
body: Check the equipment type and identification number.
Verify lifting capacity, installation conditions and manufacturer restrictions.
Check inspection records and authorisation for use.
Clarify illegible or contradictory markings.
slides.callout: Verify lifting capacity for the actual operating conditions.

slides.title: Recording and maintaining lifting equipment
body: State registration or internal recording requirements depend on the device type.
Exemption from state registration does not remove control obligations.
Maintain and repair equipment according to the established schedule.
Document inspections and the correction of defects.
slides.callout: Internal records also require clear responsibility.

slides.title: Responsibilities during crane operations
body: Supervision oversees safe operation.
The person responsible for serviceable condition organises maintenance and repair.
The person responsible for load handling organises the safe lifting operation.
The crane operator and slinger fulfil their duties and use agreed signals.
slides.callout: Responsibilities must be understood before lifting begins.

slides.title: Preparing a lift
body: Determine the load mass, centre of gravity and attachment points.
Select equipment and accessories with suitable characteristics.
Check the route, landing area and absence of people.
Agree on communication between participants.
slides.callout: Establish an unknown load mass before lifting.

slides.title: Slings and lifting accessories
body: Check identification and suitability for the chosen lifting arrangement.
Inspect ropes, chains, sling legs, hooks and connections.
Remove damaged or unidentifiable accessories from service.
Protect load edges using the specified padding.
slides.callout: A knot in a sling is not a repair.

slides.title: Lifting danger zone
body: Keep people out of the area where a load could fall or move.
Do not allow anyone beneath a suspended load.
Do not guide a load by hand while positioned between it and an obstacle.
Maintain the zone boundaries throughout the operation.
slides.callout: A short lift presents the same hazard.

slides.title: Signals and stopping
body: Agree on clear signals and the communication method in advance.
Stop movement if communication is lost.
A stop signal concerning danger to people requires an immediate response.
Resume only after the cause is resolved and actions are coordinated.
slides.callout: Do not guess the meaning of an unclear signal.

slides.title: Inspection of lifting equipment
body: Shift inspections, maintenance and technical examinations serve different purposes.
Check the structure, mechanisms, brakes and protective devices.
Determine intervals and scope from the applicable rules and equipment documentation.
Do not bypass a defective limiter to finish a shift.
slides.callout: Protective devices are part of the conditions for safe operation.

slides.title: Testing and repairing lifting equipment
body: Qualified specialists conduct tests under the established programme.
A test load does not authorise overloads during normal operation.
Certain repairs or modifications require additional examination.
Record the results and authorisation for continued operation.
slides.callout: A trial lift cannot replace the required post-repair examination.

slides.title: Welded joints in lifting equipment
body: Repair safety-critical components using an established procedure.
Determine welder, material and inspection requirements for the structure.
Cracks, deformation and unacceptable defects require specialist assessment.
Unauthorised welding can alter structural behaviour.
slides.callout: Repair of a load-bearing structure requires a specific decision.

slides.title: Scenario: a damaged sling
body: A sling is defective, but the load must be moved urgently.
Do not begin the lift; notify the responsible person.
Prevent further issue of the accessory pending the required decision.
Continue with suitable, serviceable equipment.
slides.callout: Urgency does not change acceptance criteria.

slides.title: Pressure equipment
body: Boilers, vessels, pipelines and cylinders contain stored energy.
Loss of containment can cause a release, burns or harmful exposure.
Risk depends on pressure, temperature and the working medium.
Operate each device within its established limits.
slides.callout: A small vessel is not necessarily a low-hazard vessel.

slides.title: Operating and design parameters
body: Operating, design, permitted and test pressures serve different purposes.
Test pressure applies to an established test procedure.
Use the documented and authorised operating limits.
Observe temperature restrictions and medium compatibility.
slides.callout: A test parameter is not an operating parameter.

slides.title: Vessel classification and applicable rules
body: Classification depends on parameters and the nature of the medium.
Pressure alone is insufficient for a universal assessment.
A specialist determines applicable requirements and inspection scope.
Operators use the established restrictions for their own equipment.
slides.callout: Classification affects inspection and documentation.

slides.title: Protective devices
body: Safety devices limit dangerous parameter exceedances.
Their condition and settings require established checks.
Do not bypass, blank off or alter protection without authorisation.
Investigate the cause of a protective trip.
slides.callout: Protection is not intended to compensate continually for an incorrect operating mode.

slides.title: Monitoring pressure and temperature
body: Compare instrument readings with the permitted operating conditions.
Check for visible damage and unreliable readings.
Replace a faulty instrument under the established procedure.
Respond to leakage, vibration or unusual noise as instructed.
slides.callout: One normal reading is insufficient when other danger signs are present.

slides.title: Starting and monitoring operation
body: Confirm equipment readiness and authorisation before starting.
Check valves, protection and the required instruments.
Change parameters in the sequence specified by the instructions.
Respond to deviations as instructed; do not guess settings.
slides.callout: Starting after repair requires confirmed readiness.

slides.title: Stopping and preparing for maintenance
body: Isolate equipment from pressure sources and hazardous media.
Release pressure and verify a safe condition.
Clean, purge and test the atmosphere where required.
Begin work after completing protective measures and authorisation.
slides.callout: A faulty gauge reading zero does not prove safety.

slides.title: Technical examination of vessels
body: Inspection and testing assess technical condition.
Intervals depend on the device and applicable requirements.
Do not start work when an examination is overdue; notify the responsible person to arrange the examination and authorisation.
Record the results in the equipment documentation.
slides.callout: Do not copy an inspection interval from a different vessel.

slides.title: Compressed gas cylinders
body: Identify the gas using markings and documentation.
Protect cylinders against falling, heat and valve damage.
Use compatible regulators and serviceable connections.
Never check leaks with an open flame.
slides.callout: Do not connect a cylinder with uncertain identification.

slides.title: Repairing and welding vessels
body: Repair only after safe removal from service.
The procedure, personnel and inspection must suit the vessel's purpose.
Do not weld a container with unidentified residual contents.
Return to service requires documented inspection results.
slides.callout: An apparently empty container may retain explosive residues.

slides.title: Scenario: rising pressure
body: Pressure rises and normal control fails to restore the operating conditions.
The operator follows the emergency shutdown instructions.
Move people out of danger and notify the responsible person.
Do not bypass protection or repair equipment under pressure.
slides.callout: Investigate the cause after making the situation safe.

slides.title: Electrical hazards
body: Current, electrical arcs and hot components can cause severe harm.
Moisture, damaged insulation and conductive surfaces increase danger.
The absence of sparks or noise does not establish absence of voltage.
Restrict access to electrical installations under the established procedure.
slides.callout: Voltage can remain dangerous without any advance sensation.

slides.title: Personnel categories and authority
body: Duties and electrical safety qualification groups determine permitted actions.
A group does not authorise every task without an assignment and authorisation.
Only authorised personnel connect, repair and switch equipment.
Learners must remain within the limits of their preparation.
slides.callout: Knowing a term does not authorise an operation.

slides.title: Organising work in electrical installations
body: Determine the required form of authorisation for the specific task.
Appoint responsible persons and the work team.
The person admitting the team checks workplace preparation and gives a briefing.
Record breaks, relocation and completion under the established procedure.
slides.callout: The actual work must match the assigned task.

slides.title: Work with voltage removed
body: Authorised personnel carry out the necessary disconnections.
They prevent unintended energisation and display prohibition notices.
They verify absence of voltage and install the required earthing.
They install the necessary barriers and other notices.
slides.callout: Disconnecting and verifying absence of voltage are different actions.

slides.title: Earthing and protective conductors
body: The protective conductor is part of the shock-protection system.
Repair damaged connections before work.
Do not replace a protective conductor with an improvised metal connection.
Specialists carry out checks and repairs.
slides.callout: An intact-looking enclosure does not prove effective protection.

slides.title: Portable equipment
body: Inspect the enclosure, cable, plug and connections before use.
Select equipment for the environment and follow its instructions.
Stop using equipment with a damaged cable or signs of overheating.
An improvised connection does not replace a serviceable assembly.
slides.callout: Check condition before switching on.

slides.title: Electrical protective equipment
body: Select protection for the voltage and nature of the work.
Before use, check integrity and required test markings.
Do not use damaged equipment or equipment with overdue tests.
PPE does not permit bypassing organisational measures.
slides.callout: An unknown test date requires verification.

slides.title: Work near live parts
body: Determine boundaries and safe distances for the actual installation.
Maintain them for tools, loads and equipment parts as well as people.
Do not move barriers without authorisation.
If conditions change, stop work until protective measures are reviewed.
slides.callout: Dangerous approach does not require direct contact.

slides.title: Returning electrical equipment to service
body: Verify completion and removal of people from the danger zone.
Remove temporary protective measures in the established sequence.
Record completion and authorisation to energise.
Authorised personnel carry out energisation.
slides.callout: A trial start requires the same safety controls.

slides.title: Scenario: a damaged cable
body: A portable tool has an exposed conductor.
Stop using it and prevent further energisation.
Notify the responsible person to arrange repair or replacement.
Do not touch the damage or repair the cable while energised.
slides.callout: Applying tape alone does not authorise continued use.

slides.title: Emergency notification
body: Report the location, hazard and known information about casualties.
Use the site's established communication channels; call 112 or 101 where needed.
Do not delay reporting while independently searching for the cause.
Warn nearby people without exposing yourself to danger.
slides.callout: The report must enable responders to locate the danger quickly.

slides.title: Evacuation and assembly point
body: Use a safe escape route appropriate to the hazard.
Do not return for belongings or enter a closed-off zone.
At the assembly point, report your presence and known missing persons.
Return only when authorised after conditions have been assessed.
slides.callout: Report immediately if a person's whereabouts are unknown.

slides.title: Safety when giving assistance
body: First make sure the rescuer is not exposed to danger.
Call emergency services and describe the situation.
Act within your training and follow the dispatcher's instructions.
Do not enter a hazardous atmosphere or touch an energised casualty without appropriate protection.
slides.callout: A second casualty makes rescue more difficult.

slides.title: Reviewing an event and restarting
body: Preserve information about signs, timing and circumstances.
Establish causes from facts, including organisational conditions.
Verify corrective measures before resuming work.
Inform personnel about changes to instructions and equipment.
slides.callout: Restart requires correction of the cause, not just the consequences.

slides.title: Final knowledge assessment
body: Work requires a clear task, serviceable equipment and valid authorisation.
Lifting defects, pressure leaks and electrical damage require timely stopping.
Emergency actions begin with protecting people and raising the alarm.
Select Start test.
slides.callout: If conditions are uncertain, wait for verification before working.
